title: The US- and Israel-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation says it began aid distribution in Gaza
body:
On 26 May 2025, the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF), a group backed by the United States and Israel, said it had begun operations in Gaza, delivering truckloads of food to newly established distribution sites. The Times of Israel reported that the announcement followed Hebrew media reports claiming the group had not started operating that day as planned. The GHF did not say how much aid was distributed but released photographs of Gazans collecting aid boxes at a site, and said more trucks would arrive the next day.

The foundation was created in early 2025 as Israel sought a new aid mechanism that it said would prevent diversion of supplies by Hamas. The plan called for a small number of sites in southern Gaza where pre-selected family representatives would collect food boxes in a zone secured and operated by American private contractors. The GHF named John Acree as interim executive director after his predecessor resigned on 25 May, saying Israeli restrictions prevented the group from adhering to humanitarian principles.

The GHF accused Hamas of issuing death threats against aid groups that agreed to cooperate with it and of trying to block Gazans from reaching its sites, claims the article did not independently verify. The United Nations and other international organizations in Gaza said they would not cooperate with the GHF, arguing that it violated humanitarian principles by requiring long walks and limiting distribution to southern Gaza, which they said would amount to forced displacement. Only a small number of lesser-known organizations, including the US-based Rahma Worldwide, agreed to take part.
